title: Queue file layout, cap values, valid-from parameter, queue-load approval route, overflow-refusal message ID and the publication and read surface of the P3 reference-load and queue reads and the P7 approval are not specified
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md lines 1138-1218 (RWB-AD-014 Configure queues); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md slides 14, 20, 41 and 42; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1.md slides 11, 13, 15 and 16; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
section: Section 11 Data; section 12.2 REST operations consumed; section 12.8 Contract fakes; section 14 Validation and messages
description: No source read fixes any of the following for RWB-AD-014 in the target: (1) the queue file layout and the cap values it may carry - the legacy data table names only queue id, queue_code, queue_name, team_code, role_code, assignment_method 'and 2 more' (DF-WRK-001 to DF-WRK-008), and no cap range or cap parameter is stated for a queue load; (2) the name and type of the valid-from parameter the load carries; (3) the approval route of a queue load in the target, that is how the rwb-case reference-load approval (POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve) and the rwb-decision rule-version approval (POST /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve) divide one approval, in which order they are called, and which of them writes the one decision record; (4) the message ID and text of the refusal when a queue row names an overflow queue that does not exist - the legacy story states the refusal (AC2) but its message table carries only MSG-P4-001 to MSG-P4-003, MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-P7-003, none of which is an overflow refusal; (5) the exact publication and read surface of the P3 reference-load and queue reads and of the P7 approval, that is the response field names for loadId, versionId, table version, valid from, author, approver, rule id and rule version on POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads, POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve, GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues, POST /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/placements, GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}, POST /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve and GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log, and whether the approval is announced by one rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 on rwb.decision-record.v1 only.
evidence: RWB-AD-014: queue row 'id, queue_code, queue_name, team_code, role_code, assignment_method and 2 more' (DF-WRK-001 to DF-WRK-008); Endpoints table lists only GET /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions and POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve, with no reference-load and no queue read; Validation and messages table lists MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003, MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-P7-003 and no overflow message; AC2 states only 'the system refuses the load'. ownership.json gives POST /admin/reference-loads and POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve to P3 under ruling ASM-A6-api-4 and POST /admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve to P3-to-P7 under ruling ASM-A6-api-3, and neither entry states how the two approvals compose. Arch v5 slides 14, 20, 41 and 42 name no queue-load operation, no cap and no valid-from parameter.
area: Integration harness: queue reference data, reference-load surface, rule-version approval and decision-record publication
proposed: Publish with the P3 and P7 contract stories: the queue file layout with its required columns and the cap value or range it may carry; the valid-from parameter name and type; one named approval route for a queue load that states the order of POST /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/approve and POST /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-versions/{versionId}/approve and which one writes the single decision record; an overflow-refusal message ID and its text; and the response schemas of the seven P3 and P7 operations named above, including the field names for loadId, versionId, table version, valid from, author, approver, rule id, rule version and the ledger confirmation, with the one DecisionRecorded publication on rwb.decision-record.v1.

title: RWB-AD-015: the service-level file and its warning layout, the valid-from parameter name, the approval route, the exact timer projection fields, the refusal message ID and the running-timer recompute rule are not published
source: Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3, RWB-AD-015, lines 1220 to 1300 (story, AC1 and AC2, data, endpoints, permission checks, validation and messages); Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 rows for timer, rule_row, parameter_catalog, parameter_value, reference_version, reference_row, decision_log_entry and the six API rows; Architecture v5 slides 14, 41, 42 and 44; Temporal and Drools design slides 13 and 24
description: No source read names the layout of the service-level file or of its warning (whether the allowed time and the warning point sit in one parameter_value row, in a rule_row timer_spec, or in a reference_row payload), the parameter key that carries the valid-from date, or which of the P3 and P7 operations is the approval route for a service level as against a rule version. The exact fields of the timer projection behind GET /cases/{caseId}/timers are not listed either, so the rule version stamp the proof reads on a running timer is assumed and not specified. The message ID a refused service-level load answers (a state code the reference list does not hold, or a row without its allowed time) is not published, and neither is the rule that decides when a running timer is recomputed when a new version takes effect. The run therefore asserts the refusal and the absence of a version instead of a message string, reads the projection as expires_at, warn_at, status and rule version, and reports the recompute path as not exercised.
evidence: Legacy story lines 1250 to 1263 gives only the entity and field ranges (recovery_case, timer, rule_row) and two endpoints; lines 1279 to 1287 gives five messages, none of them for a service-level load; the Ownership Map rules the timer as the P3 projection and the rule rows to P7 without publishing a projection field list; Architecture v5 slide 42 retires TimerDue and keeps TimerBreached without naming the projection; the Temporal design slides 13, 15 and 24 describe the durable timer and the four workflow steps without a service-level file or recompute rule.
proposed: Publish the service-level file and warning layout, the valid-from parameter key, the approval route for a service level, the timer projection field list with its rule version stamp, the refusal message for a service-level load, and the recompute rule; until then the harness holds the state code, the allowed time, the warning point and the valid-from dates as fixture data, reads the projection as expires_at, warn_at, status and rule version, and asserts the refusal without a message ID.

title: The job read, the rerun answer, the job-log fields, the freshness answer, the v_ace_batch_status read path and the two refusal messages of the interface and job monitor are not published
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Administration Stories v3.md, RWB-AD-018 Interface and job monitor (lines 1502-1548); Ownership Map v1 API rows for GET /admin/jobs, POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun and GET /data-products/freshness; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15, 41 and 44
section: §3 Preconditions; §5 X3 and X4; §7 AC2 and AC5; §11 Data; §12.8 Contract fakes; §13 Solution plan; §14 Validation and messages; §15 Screens and states
description: The legacy story publishes three operations (GET /admin/jobs, POST /admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun, GET /data-products/freshness), the job_catalog, data_product_load and v_ace_batch_status entities, and three messages (MSG-P1-001, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002), but no source read specifies six things the harness must assert: the response shape of the job read (job ID, business date, status, duration, each check result and the run number); the response shape of the rerun (the run it started, its number and status); the field list of the job log that must hold both runs of one rerun and the repeated Idempotency-Key; the exact shape of the freshness answer (each source, its last complete ACE business date, the product state, the last refresh date and the unknown-freshness case); the path by which P1 reads v_ace_batch_status behind that answer; and the message IDs for a refused rerun and for an ACE source batch named as not a Workbench job. The run asserts all six through the owner's contract, so the shapes and the two message IDs must be fixed before the story can be Done.
evidence: Legacy story lines 1502-1508 name the entities and field IDs of the catalog, the load and the view but no field list for any read answer and no job-log field set; lines 1510-1516 name the three paths only; lines 1531-1537 publish MSG-P1-001, MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-P4-002 and no message for a refused rerun or a batch that is not a Workbench job; Architecture v5 slide 15 line 1075 lists GET /freshness only, slide 41 line 2884 names the owner and the schema, and slide 44 lines 2980-2981 name JOB-04 and its mechanism without a response; the Ownership Map v1 API rows name P1 as owner of the three operations and publish no schema.
proposed: P1 rwb-source-data publishes four schemas in its OpenAPI and AsyncAPI documents at the wave 4 entry check — the job read with its job-log fields and run number, the rerun answer, the freshness answer with its unknown-freshness case, and the v_ace_batch_status read path behind it — and the message catalogue adds the refused-rerun and not-a-Workbench-job messages; until then the harness asserts each answer field by field from the published contract and cites this row.

title: The data quality console read shapes, the gateway-bff route specification, the refresh cadence and the unreachable-read message are not stated in any source
source: Template and Rules v1 §R9; Architecture v5 slides 15, 41 and 44; Ownership Map rows GET /data-products/freshness and GET /admin/jobs; legacy RWB-AD-019 endpoints note (lines 1599 to 1601)
section: 3 Preconditions; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.6 Schedules; 14 Validation and messages
description: No source read fixes the path, the paging, the query parameters or the response field shape of the rwb-source-data reconciliation read behind REC-01 to REC-05 and of the business-key resolution read behind REC-05; the freshness read is named only as GET /freshness on slide 15 and as the Ownership Map row GET /data-products/freshness, with no field shape for the business date, the batch state and the last complete ACE business date. The gateway-bff composite route behind SCR-45 has no path, no merge rule for the three blocks, no per-call timeout ownership and no rule for which block wins when two answers disagree, and the rwb-case console route adds no response or error envelope of its own. The stale-set refresh cadence (15 minutes used here) is a design default with no source value, and no message ID exists for an unreachable or timed-out P1 read, so the console and the harness have no text to assert for that path.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 15 lists only 'REST GET /freshness (business date)' for rwb-source-data and states no reconciliation or key-resolution path; slide 44 gives JOB-04 as 'event-triggered workflow' with no output shape; ownership.json holds GET /data-products/freshness and GET /admin/jobs for P1 with no schema; the legacy story says 'No endpoint in this story' and lists no read path; the P3 slice of this key records the same gap for its three reads and its route.
proposed: Publish in the rwb-source-data contract the reconciliation read, the key-resolution read and the freshness read with their paths, paging and field shapes; publish the gateway-bff SCR-45 route with its path, parallel merge rules and per-call timeout ownership; fix the refresh cadence as platform configuration; and add a problem-response code and text for an unreachable P1 read. Until then the harness pins the operation and the shape it uses and fails the hop on a mismatch.

title: Partner portal route, firm-scope resolution and partner session are not specified by any source read
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17 (partner portal /partner/v1/* FAPI 2.0, partner gateway, MFA); Ownership Map v1 (ASM-A6-tables-6, partner_user); Legacy RWB-AD-022 (Administration Stories v3 lines 1792-1864); Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 (DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217)
description: No source read for RWB-AD-022 specifies the partner portal route and how the firm scope is resolved on it: the gateway route the partner identity uses, the name of the firm-scope field on GET /partner/v1/partners and GET /partner/v1/partner/instructions, and whether a client-supplied firm parameter is refused or ignored with its answer. No source specifies the shape of the partner session and of the MFA assertion at the partner gateway, so the run can assert the presence of the internal role and of Partner portal R and of a second factor but not a claim set or a field name. No source publishes the partner_user field set as an API answer, and none states that rwb-access answers no partner user, so AC5 is asserted from the session answer shape and the published contract set only. No source states the answer or any message a cross-firm instruction identifier receives: 404 with no instruction detail is assumed, and no business message exists for it, so the run asserts the status and the absence of detail.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 17 says only 'Partner portal: /partner/v1/* (FAPI 2.0)' and 'via partner gateway, MFA'; slide 41 lists partner users as S9 data with no API shape; the legacy story lists two endpoints and two messages (MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P4-002) and no cross-firm path; ASM-A6-tables-6 rules that P4 holds no partner user but defines no answer shape.
area: Integration harness, S9 partner portal, P4 session
proposed: Fix the portal route specification, the firm-scope field name and the refusal-or-ignore rule for a client-supplied firm in the S9 CON story; pin the partner session and MFA assertion shape in the P4 session contract; publish whether any partner-user read exists on any contract; and fix the cross-firm answer (404 with no detail) and whether it carries a message. Until then the harness holds each as configuration and asserts status and absence only.
